findings.text: Exposes a ratelimited dirty balancing entry for an address space that resolves backing writeback state, derives an allowance from per task progress and global pressure, absorbs previously leaked dirtied counts, and delegates to the main throttling loop when the allowance is reached.
Exposes a convenience wrapper that invokes the flagged ratelimited balancer with no special options.
Exposes a background threshold predicate that evaluates global state and, when valid, memory cgroup state, reporting true if either domain exceeds its background level.
Exposes a tagging service that marks dirty entries as intended for writeback across a caller supplied index range while cooperatively yielding the processor during long scans.

Exposes an iterator that initializes writeback traversal on first call, optionally tags candidate pages, then yields successive eligible folios until quota exhaustion, completion, or integrity specific termination, preserving cyclic resume position and first error.

Exposes a writeback driver that estimates bandwidth, dispatches to filesystem writepages when present, retries allocation failure under full synchronization with reclaim throttling, and refreshes bandwidth observations periodically.
Exposes a cleaning accounting service that reverses dirty related counters for a folio size amount, including file dirty, zone pending, reclaimable, donotcache when applicable, and task IO.

Boot time initialization that prepares the global writeback domain, registers online and dead processor callbacks for ratelimit maintenance, and registers virtual memory writeback controls when configuration enables them.

Freerun status indicates operation below a ceiling derived from normal and background thresholds, using writeback scoped counters under strict limits and domain counters otherwise, with an additional local throttle task exemption evaluated against writeback scoped ceiling.
Exceeded status requires writeback dirty beyond writeback threshold together with either domain dirty beyond domain threshold or strict limit mode enabled.
Poll interval selection uses writeback dirty and threshold under strict limits and domain dirty and threshold otherwise.

Writeback dirty observation uses exact summed counters when thresholds are small relative to statistical error, and cheaper approximate counters otherwise, adding reclaimable and writeback components for the main limit and reclaimable alone for background evaluation.

Main throttling loop alternates between free running and paced states. Free running applies when global and applicable memory cgroup domains allow it and refreshes per task pause allowance from poll intervals. Paced operation ensures background writeback activity, selects the more constrained domain by position ratio, derives task rate from global rate and ratio, bounds sleep duration, honors asynchronous requests without sleeping, and exits on allowance, error bound, or fatal signal.

Writeback traversal maintains initialization, fetching, accounting, and completion states. Initialization sets start index from cyclic resume or range start and tags when required. Fetching locks candidates and discards ineligible ones. Accounting decrements remaining work and treats errors and quota differently for integrity versus background modes. Completion releases batch resources and updates cyclic resume.

A folio is eligible only when still attached to the expected mapping and marked dirty, with concurrent writeback causing deferral under relaxed synchronization and waiting under full synchronization, followed by an atomic transition clearing dirty for IO that may still decline the folio.

Tagging holds the page cache array lock with interrupts disabled and periodically drops it to schedule. Fetching holds each folio lock across eligibility checks and releases before retry. Ratelimit and leak per processor updates run with preemption disabled.

Observed throttle control carries domain dirty, threshold and background threshold alongside writeback scoped dirty, threshold and background threshold plus derived freerun flag, exceeded flag, position ratio, and references to writeback and domain state.

Observed writeback control carries synchronization mode, tagging and cyclic flags, current and resume indexes, range bounds, remaining work count, saved and current error, folio batch, and owning mapping linkage used during iteration.

Background pressure evaluation refreshes available dirty and limits, compares domain dirty against domain background threshold, then computes a writeback scoped background threshold and compares writeback dirty against it.

Dirtied accounting increments file dirty, zone pending, dirtied, reclaimable and dirtied writeback counters plus task IO and per task and per processor ratelimit contributions, with an extra donotcache component for dropbehind folios. Cleaned accounting reverses the corresponding subset.

Throttling hazards include per processor allowance overflow with many simultaneous dirtier tasks, escape by short lived tasks mitigated by leak absorption, sleeping in killable state with timeout, asynchronous callers receiving a retryable failure instead of sleeping, unresponsive server starvation mitigated by an error sized writeback allowance, and allocation failure retry limited to full synchronization.

Virtual memory controls expose dirty background ratio and bytes, dirty ratio and bytes, writeback and expire intervals in centiseconds, high memory dirtyable on supporting builds, and a deprecated laptop mode that warns and ignores writes. Ratio controls span zero to one hundred and byte controls enforce minima.
Minimum dirty bytes equals two pages. Per processor dirty throttle leak counter initializes to zero. The asynchronous balance option uses flag BDP_ASYNC and reports EAGAIN instead of sleeping.
Changing the periodic writeback interval to a new nonzero value wakes flusher threads for immediate effect, while zero disables periodic activity.
Processor online and dead callbacks refresh global ratelimit state and report success.
